clauses.text: Prices as per the price annex, fixed for each calendar year. Changes require written notice of at least 60 days before the end of the calendar year.
Delivery DAP; standard lead time 10 days from order.
The quality agreement applies: on-time delivery target 95 %, flat fee of EUR 150 per supplier-caused complaint.
Valid from 2024-01-01 to 2026-12-31; extends by 12 months unless terminated with 60 days' notice.

persona.summary: Family steel stockholder (196 M EUR, 500 staff); we are 0.22 % but it twice called us an important reference customer. Cheaper second source for C45 bar (126.05 vs 70740's 143.39) and sole source for S235 sheet. Proposes a PPI-C241 adjustment clause for the sheet; owner offered open-book costing twice. History: passes on more decrease than it asks (kept 155 %). Accept a two-way clause, push the base price with its own cost shares.
persona.notes: Needs an index clause to protect its steel margin and wants to keep a reference customer. No hedge stated. Our spend fell ~9 % in FY2026. Contradiction: 0.22 % share vs 'important reference customer'. OTD 90-92 % vs 95 % target, 1 open 8D.
fears: steel cost risk without an index clause

evidence.quote: Stahlhandel Rupprecht-Kessel GmbH said Hollerau is an important reference customer for them.
he offered to walk us through their calculation (hourly rates and material) if that helps to settle prices.
including a price adjustment clause based on PPI-C241. Please let us know your view.

arguments: its own cost shares from the open-book calculation
no index argument: its cost drivers rose over 12 months (PPI-C2431 +12.3 %, PPI-C241 +6.5 %, LCI-C +2.7 %)
avoid: citing a cost driver that rose
changing terms after its final offer
mandatory_terms: PPI-C241 price adjustment clause (it proposed one for the sheet)
tactics: Accept its PPI-C241 clause but set it two-way with our base month, material share and a deadband.
Take up the owner's offer: ask for its calculation and argue from its own material and labour shares.
Use its reference-customer statement as the reason for a sharp base price.
Cite the scorecard once (OTD 92 % vs 95 %, 1 open 8D).
Do not change any term after its final offer.
playbook.expected_concession: No arena data; history shows it settles below its own ask every year (kept 155 %), so expect it to move further than its first counter.
